stem: A child with cystic fibrosis has a Class III mutation; which therapy is best matched to this mutation class?
explanation: Ivacaftor is the best match for a Class III cystic fibrosis mutation because it is a potentiator that improves channel opening.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because ivacaftor is a potentiator used for Class III mutations, which have a channel opening defect.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because lumacaftor is a corrector and is not the specific therapy for Class III channel opening defects.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because elexacaftor is a corrector and is not the singled-out treatment for Class III mutations.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because fat-soluble vitamins are part of general cystic fibrosis management, not mutation-specific therapy.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because nebulised antibiotics treat airway infection and lung disease, not the underlying CFTR mutation defect.
